Rashi on Sotah 18b:10:1.hebrew: נשואין הראשונים - כגון גירשה והחזירה, וקינא לה ונסתרה:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:10:1.english: The first marriage - For example, he divorced her and remarried her, and he warned her and she secluded herself.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:10:2.hebrew: [על נשואי אחיו] מהו - לגלגל זנות שתחת אחיו. דהא דתנן במתניתין: ארוסה ונשואה, שומרת יבם וכנוסה — לאו בחדא אתתא קאי, שישקנה יבם וישביענה על האירוסין ונישואין של אחיו; אלא מילי מילי קתני: אם הבעל משקה, מתנה עמה על ארוסה ונשואה, ואם היבם שכנסה משקה, מתנה עמה שומרת יבם וכנוסה:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:10:2.english: [Regarding his brother's marriage] what is the law? - [Is it permitted] to carry over the infidelity that occurred under his brother [onto the yavam's account]? For [consider] what we learned in the Mishnah: "betrothed and married, a woman awaiting levirate marriage and one who was taken in levirate marriage." This does not refer to a single woman, such that the yavam would give her to drink and have her swear concerning the betrothal and marriage of his brother. Rather, it teaches separate matters: If the husband gives her to drink, he stipulates with her regarding [her status as] betrothed and married; and if the yavam who took her in levirate marriage gives her to drink, he stipulates with her regarding [her status as] a woman awaiting levirate marriage and one taken in levirate marriage.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:11:1.hebrew: הא אסירה הכי נמי דמתנה - וזו נאסרת עליו בזנות נישואין הראשונים לעולם, וכן בזנות נישואי אחיו, כדאמר בפ"ק (לעיל סוטה דף ב.): ואם מת חולצת ולא מתייבמת:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:11:1.english: But [if she is] forbidden, so too he stipulates - And this one [the *shomeret yavam*, who is awaiting levirate marriage] becomes forbidden to him, [through] adultery during the first marriage, forever; and likewise [through] adultery during the marriage of his brother, as is stated in the first chapter (above, Sotah 2a): "And if he dies, she performs *chalitzah* and is not taken in levirate marriage."

Rashi on Sotah 18b:12:1.english: Not like when R. Meir said, "Amen, that I will not become defiled" - It occurred to him that she should be examined now with regard to the future.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:12:2.hebrew: מערערין אותה - חוזרין לה לתוך גרונה כאדם הנחנק ע"י משקה, נראה כעושה ערער, והוא לשון זעקת שבר, יעוערו (ישעיהו טו):
Rashi on Sotah 18b:12:2.english: They "stir up" her [throat] - [The water] comes back up into her throat, like a person who chokes on a drink and appears to be making a rasping sound ("arar"). It is an expression of a cry of anguish, as in "they shall raise [a cry of destruction]" (Isaiah 15).

Rashi on Sotah 18b:13:1.hebrew: על נשואין אחרונים - לר"מ דאמר מתנה על העתיד, מהו שיתנה עמה בגלגול שבועה שלא תטמא אם יגרשנה ויחזירנה ותטמא:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:13:1.english: Regarding later marriages - According to R. Meir, who said that one may stipulate regarding the future: What is the law as to whether he may stipulate with her, by way of an extension of the oath, that she will not become defiled [i.e., commit adultery] if he divorces her and remarries her, and she [then] becomes defiled?

Rashi on Sotah 18b:14:1.hebrew: ואחר כך יחזירנה - טעמא דתטמא בימי גירושיה, דלא מיתסרא עליה. הא תטמא לאחר חזרה, הכי נמי דמתני עכשיו:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:14:1.english: And afterward he remarries her - The reason [that the stipulation does not apply] is that she became impure during the days of her divorce, when she was not forbidden to him. [But] if she were to become impure after her return, then indeed, he can stipulate now [about that].

Rashi on Sotah 18b:15:1.hebrew: תורת הקנאות - תורה אחת לכל הקנאות, שבכולן יעשה לה כתורה הזאת:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:15:1.english: The law of jealousies - One law for all [cases of] jealousies; in all of them, he shall do to her according to this law.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר "זאת" - מיעוטא הוא, "זאת" ולא אחרת:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: "This" - It is an exclusion: "this" and not another.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:2.hebrew: חופר שיחין - להכניס מים לעולי רגלים בשדות ובדרכים:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:2.english: One who digs ditches - To bring in water for the pilgrims [who go up to Jerusalem for the festivals] in the fields and on the roads.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:3.hebrew: בשני אנשים - אם מת בעלה זה שהשקה, ונישאת לאחר, וקינא לה, והיא נסתרה, וקבלנו עדותו של נחוניא שישקנה השני. דרבי יהודה דריש "זאת" למעוטי שאינה שותה ושונה על ידי בעל א', אם חזר וקינא לה; ודריש "תורת" לרבות ששותה פעם שניה על ידי בעל שני. ומדקאמר ר' יהודה דע"י בעל שני חוזרת ושותה, מכלל דלתנא קמא אפילו בעל א' משקה שני פעמים. והיינו דפרכינן: ותנא קמא, הא כתיב "זאת", ומאי קא ממעט מיניה:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:16:3.english: With two men - If her husband who gave her the water to drink died, and she married another, and he warned her, and she secluded herself, and we accepted the testimony of Nechunya that the second husband should give her the water to drink. For Rabbi Yehuda expounds "this" to exclude the possibility that she drinks a second time through one husband, if he again warned her; and he expounds "law of" to include that she drinks a second time through a second husband. And since Rabbi Yehuda says that through a second husband she goes back and drinks, it follows that according to the first Tanna, even one husband gives her to drink twice. This is what we ask: "But the first Tanna — it is written 'this,' so what does he exclude from it?"

Rashi on Sotah 18b:1:1.hebrew: שומרת יבם וכנוסה - ואם היתה יבמתו וכנסה, וקינא לה ונסתרה, מגלגל עליה שבועה שלא נטמאת כשהיא שומרת יבם. שומרת יבם — מצפה וממתנת ליבם שייבמנה, כמו "ואביו שמר את הדבר" (בראשית ל״ז:י״א), "לא תשמור על חטאתי" (איוב י״ד:ט״ז):
Rashi on Sotah 18b:1:1.english: A woman awaiting her yavam, and one who has been taken in marriage - And if she was his yavam (his brother's widow) and he married her, and he warned her and she secluded herself [with another man], he extends the oath to her [also] that she did not become defiled while she was awaiting her yavam. "Awaiting her yavam" means she looks forward and waits for her yavam to perform levirate marriage with her, like "And his father kept [shamar] the matter" (Genesis 37:11), [and] "You will not watch [tishmor] over my sin" (Job 14:16).

Rashi on Sotah 18b:1:2.hebrew: אמן שלא נטמאתי - היינו קבלת שבועה. ״ואם נטמאתי יבאו בי״ — היינו קבלת אלה, כדרך שהשביעה, כדאמר לעיל בגמרא: ״משביעני עליך שלא נטמאת, ואם נטמאת יבאו ביך״. והיינו פירושו דאמן על השבועה, אמן על האלה, דתניא ברישא:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:1:2.english: Amen, that I have not been defiled - This is the acceptance of the oath. "And if I have been defiled, [the curses] shall come upon me" — this is the acceptance of the curse, in the manner that he adjured her, as stated earlier in the Gemara: "I adjure you that you have not been defiled, and if you have been defiled, [the curses] shall come upon you." And this is its meaning: "Amen" on the oath, "Amen" on the curse, as was taught in the first clause.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:2:1.hebrew: אמן שלא אטמא - שאם תטמא לאחר זמן, מים מערערין אותה לאחר שתטמא, כדתניא בברייתא בגמרא:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:2:1.english: Amen, that I have not become defiled - For if she becomes defiled at a later time, the waters test her after she has become defiled, as it is taught in the baraita in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:3:1.hebrew: ולא על אחר שתתגרש כו' - ואפילו לר"מ דאמר מתנה על העתיד:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:3:1.english: Nor for after she is divorced, etc. - Even according to Rabbi Meir, who said that one may stipulate regarding the future.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:4:1.hebrew: ונטמאת - בגירושיה, דאינה נאסרת עליו לחזור לו אלא אם כן נישאת על ידי קידושין. דכי כתיב (דברים כד) "לא יוכל בעלה הראשון אשר שלחה לשוב לקחתה" — אחר קידושין ונישואין כתיב, כדכתיב "והיתה לאיש אחר ושנאה האיש האחרון":
Rashi on Sotah 18b:4:1.english: And she became defiled - This refers to [the time of] her divorce, for she is not forbidden to return to him [her first husband] unless she was married [to another] through betrothal. For when it is written (Deuteronomy 24), "Her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again," it is written [only] with regard to [a case that follows] betrothal and marriage, as it is written, "and she becomes another man's wife, and the latter man hates her."

Rashi on Sotah 18b:6:1.english: That she committed adultery - While she was a widow awaiting her yavam (levirate brother-in-law).

Rashi on Sotah 18b:6:2.english: Forbidden to her yavam - Like a woman who committed adultery while married to her husband, who is forbidden to her husband.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:6:3.hebrew: מדקתני שומרת יבם - שמשביעה על זנות שזינתה כשהיא שומרת יבם:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:6:3.english: From the fact that it teaches "a woman awaiting levirate marriage" - That he administers the oath to her regarding adultery that she committed while she was awaiting levirate marriage.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:7:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא - זנתה נאסרת עליו, משום הכי מתנה ע"י גלגול אף על אותו זנות. אלא אי אמרת כו':
Rashi on Sotah 18b:7:1.english: If you say, granted - [that if] she committed adultery she is forbidden to him, therefore he may stipulate with her by means of a transmission [of the oath] even concerning that [act of] adultery. But if you say, etc.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:9:1.hebrew: אין קידושין תופסין - לאשה האסורה על המקדשה בלאו. ורבנן פליגי עליה ואמרי: בחייבי כריתות הוא דלא תפסי, אבל בחייבי לאוין תפסי. אלמא, לר"ע משוי חייבי לאוין חמורות לענין איסוריהם כחייבי כריתות, שהולד ממזר. ולגבי לאסור על בעלה נמי, כי היכי דהבא על אשת איש שהיא בכרת אסורה על בעלה, כן הבא על שומרת יבם נמי, שהיא עליו בלא תהיה אשת המת החוצה לאיש זר (דברים כה), אוסרה על יבמה:
Rashi on Sotah 18b:9:1.english: Betrothal does not take effect - with a woman who is forbidden to the one who betrothed her by a negative commandment. But the Rabbis disagree with him and say: Betrothal fails to take effect only with those liable to karet, but with those liable for [violating] negative commandments, betrothal does take effect. Evidently, according to Rabbi Akiva, he makes those liable for negative commandments as severe as those liable to karet with regard to their prohibitions — [namely,] that the offspring is a mamzer. And [he does so] with regard to forbidding her to her husband as well: just as one who has relations with a married woman, who is [forbidden] on pain of karet, renders her forbidden to her husband, so too one who has relations with a woman awaiting her yavam, who is forbidden to him by [the verse] "The wife of the deceased shall not be outside, to a strange man" (Deuteronomy 25), renders her forbidden to her yavam.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:9:2.english: And he renders her - like those who are liable for [transgressing] negative commandments.

Rashi on Sotah 18b:9:3.english: As a forbidden relation (ervah) - [Meaning, as an ervah] that carries the punishment of karet.

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:13:1.hebrew: מהו שיתנה אדם על נישואין האחרונים - ירושלמי: א"ר ינאי: פשיטא שאדם מוחל על קינוי; גירש — כמי שמחל? היך עבידא? קינא לה וגירשה, החזירה ונסתרה: אי תימא גירש כמי שמחל — צריך לקנאות לה פעם שניה; אי תימא גירש כמי שלא מחל — אין צריך לקנאות לה פעם שניה. אבל אם קינא לה ונסתרה, וידע בה, וגירשה והחזירה ונסתרה, שתתה ולא בדקו אותה המים — טהורה היא, או מאחר שאין המים בודקין את האשה — טמאה היא ואסורה לביתה:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:13:1.english: What is the law [as to whether] a man may stipulate regarding the latter marriage - The Yerushalmi [says]: Rabbi Yannai said: It is obvious that a person can forgo [his right to issue] a warning; [does] divorcing [her] count as having forgone it? How does this work? He warned her and divorced her, [then] remarried her and she secluded herself [with the man]: If you say that divorcing is like forgoing, he must warn her a second time; if you say that divorcing is like not forgoing, he need not warn her a second time. But if he warned her and she secluded herself, and he had relations with her, and he divorced her and remarried her and she secluded herself [again], [and] she drank and the water did not test her — is she pure, or, since the water does not test the woman, is she defiled and forbidden to her home?

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:16:1.hebrew: אין האשה שותה ושונה - ירושלמי: כורכמית תוכיח, ששתתה ושינתה ושילשה לפני שמעיה ואבטליון:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:16:1.english: A woman does not drink and drink again - The Jerusalem Talmud [says]: Kurkemit proves [otherwise], for she drank, and drank a second time, and drank a third time, before Shemaya and Avtalyon.

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:16:2.hebrew: קבלנו עדותו בשני אנשים - צ"ע בפ"ק דקידושין (דף יח.), דמוקמינן התם הא דקתני בגניבתו: "כיון שנמכר פעם אחת, שוב אי אתה רשאי למוכרו" — בשני בני אדם, אבל באדם אחד נמכר ונשנה. [ולפירוש רש"י התם ניחא שפיר, כיון שנמכר פעם אחת וכו'] מתוספת רבי:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:16:2.english: "We accepted his testimony with two men" - This requires further study. In the first chapter of Kiddushin (18a), we establish that what is taught there regarding [a thief sold] for his theft — "Once he has been sold one time, you may not sell him again" — [refers to selling him] to two different people, but to one person he may be sold again and again. [And according to Rashi's explanation there, it works out well, since once he was sold one time, etc.] From the addition of Rabbi [...].

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:18:1.hebrew: ורבנן בתראי הכתיב תורת - וא"ת, הא דרשינן ליה בפ"ב דכריתות (דף ט:) שאדם מביא קרבן אחד, אפילו אם קינא לאשתו על ידי אנשים הרבה? וי"ל, דהתם מיירי קודם ששתתה: קינא לה מפלוני ונסתרה, וקינא לה מפלוני ונסתרה, וכן פעמים הרבה — משקה בפעם אחת על כולן, ומביא מנחה אחת על כולן, ונפקא לן מ"קנאות". אבל הכא דרשינן "תורת" לשותה ושונה, שחזר וקינא לה לאחר שתיה ונסתרה — שחוזרת ושותה שנית:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:18:1.english: "And the later Rabbis — but it is written 'torat'" - And if you ask: Surely we expound this [word] in the second chapter of Keritot (9b) [to teach] that a person brings only one offering, even if he warned his wife regarding many men? And one can answer that there [the case] is speaking of before she drank: he warned her about so-and-so and she secluded herself, and warned her about another and she secluded herself, and so on many times — he gives her to drink once for all of them, and brings one meal-offering for all of them, and we derive this from [the plural] "kena'ot" ("jealousies"). But here we expound "torat" as referring to a woman who drinks and drinks again — [meaning] that he warned her again after she drank and she secluded herself — that she drinks a second time.

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:2:1.hebrew: אמן שלא אטמא - ירושלמי: לא שהיה ר"מ אומר "המים בודקין אותה מעכשיו", אלא "המים פקודים בה"; לכשתטמא — המים בודקין אותה למפרע:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:2:1.english: "Amen, that I have not become defiled" - [It says in] the Yerushalmi: It is not that Rabbi Meir was saying, "The water examines her from now on," but rather, "The water is appointed over her"; when she becomes defiled, the water examines her retroactively:

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:6:1.hebrew: שומרת יבם שזינתה אסורה ליבמה - פי' אפי' לרבנן דאמרי קידושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין, ופליגי אדר"ע, הכא מודו; כדאמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צב:), דכתיב בה: "לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה לאיש זר" — לא תהא בה הויה לזר. אלמא דקרא משוי לה כערוה, דלא תפסי בה קידושין, משום דאגידא ביה, והויא כארוסתו שזינתה:
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:6:1.english: A woman awaiting her yavam who committed adultery is forbidden to her yavam - Explanation: Even according to the Rabbis, who say that betrothal takes effect with those forbidden by a negative commandment (and who disagree with R. Akiva), here they agree. As stated in [the chapter] "HaIshah Rabbah" (Yevamot 92b), where it is written: "The wife of the dead man shall not be [married] outside to a stranger" — [meaning,] there shall be no [marital] status in her for a stranger. Evidently, the verse treats her like a forbidden relation (ervah) with whom betrothal does not take effect, because she is bound to him [the yavam], and she is like his betrothed who committed adultery:

Tosafot on Sotah 18b:8:1.hebrew: אמרי במערבא לית הילכתא כרב המנונא - בסוף פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף יז:) מפרש דאמרי במערבא היינו רבי ירמיה. ונראה, אע"ג דפסיק דלית הילכתא כרב המנונא, הילכתא כוותיה, דאמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צב:) דרב סבירא ליה דאין קידושין תופסין ביבמה, ושמואל מספקא ליה ואמר: בעניותינו צריכה גט, ופסיק אמימר כשמואל. ורב גידל אמר רב חייא בר יוסף אמר רב: נישואין יש בה בזנות, כדרב המנונא. וכן ר' יוחנן ור' ינאי סבירא להו התם דאין קידושין תופסין ביבמה, ופשיט לה ר' יוחנן ממתני' דלאחר שיחלוץ ליך יבמיך. וא"ל רבי ינאי: אי לאו דדלאי לך חספא, מי משכחת מרגניתא תותיה? וא"ל ר"ל לר"י: אי לאו דקלסך גברא רבה, ה"א מתני' ר"ע היא. ומיהו ר"ל לא פליג אדר' יוחנן, דהא מוקי התם באותו הפרק (דף צה.) הא דקתני "ומה במקום שבא על האיסור קל נאסר האוסר" בשומרת יבם, וכדרב המנונא ובסוף ההיא גמרא. ובשילהי החולץ (יבמות דף מט:) אנן נמי, אביי מספקא ליה אי כרב אי כשמואל. ובפ' הזורק בגיטין (דף פ:) פליגי לישני דגמרא אי מתני' הוה תיובתא לרב המנונא אי הוה סייעתיה, והתם מצי למידחי סייעתיה כי הכא, לאוקמיה מתניתין כר"ע, אלא דדחי לה מלישנא דמתני' גופיה. בירושלמי מפרש היאך קילס רבי ינאי לרבי יוחנן, שקרא עליו: "הזלים זהב מכיס", "בני אל יליזו מעיניך", "חכם בני ושמח לבי", "תן לחכם ויחכם עוד", "ישמע חכם ויוסף לקח". א"ל ר"ל: בתר כל אלו פסוקי קילוסיה, יכול הוא, פתר ליה כר"ע. ותו דחי ליה התם: ויתיבניה, מה איכפת לו ממזר גבי קינוי? התורה אמרה "וקנא את אשתו" — אפילו מקצת אשתו. ולפום מסקנא דהתם משמע דלית הילכתא כרב המנונא. והכי גרס התם: שומרת יבם שזינתה, ר"א אומר: מותרת לביתה; ר' יהושע בן לוי אומר: אסורה לביתה. א"ר ינאי: שומרת יבם שזינתה מותרת לביתה, ותני כן: "ונעלמה מעיני אישה" — ולא מעיני יבמה. רבי יעקב בן זבדי בשם ר' אבהו: מעשה היה, וכהנת היתה, והותרה לביתה. א"ר יוסי בר בון: אף לא מכות אין בה. לפי הירושלמי משמע דפליג רבי ינאי ארבי ינאי הא דאמר בהאשה רבה: א"ר ינאי, בחבורה נמנו וגמרו אין קידושין תופסין ביבמה. גרסי' הכי בירושלמי: א"ר שמואל, לא כן א"ר ינאי: נמנו שלשים וכמה זקנים — מנין שאין קדושין תופסין וכו':
Tosafot on Sotah 18b:8:1.english: "They say in the West: The halakhah is not like Rav Hamnuna" - At the end of the first chapter of Sanhedrin (17b), [the Gemara] explains that "they say in the West" refers to Rabbi Yirmeyah. And it appears that even though [Rabbi Yirmeyah] ruled that the halakhah is not like Rav Hamnuna, the halakhah is in accordance with him [Rav Hamnuna], as it says in [the chapter] Ha-Ishah Rabbah (Yevamot 92b): Rav holds that betrothal does not take effect with a yevamah, while Shmuel was uncertain about it and said: In our poverty [i.e., in our limited understanding], she requires a get; and Amemar ruled like Shmuel. And Rav Gidel said in the name of Rav Chiya bar Yosef, who said in the name of Rav: Marriage applies to her in the case of licentiousness, like Rav Hamnuna. And so too Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yannai hold there that betrothal does not take effect with a yevamah, and Rabbi Yochanan resolved it from our mishnah: "After he performs *chalitzah* for you, [your yavam is permitted to you]" - and Rabbi Yannai said to him: Had I not lifted a potsherd for you, would you have found a pearl beneath it? And Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan: Were it not that a great man praised you, I would have said [that] the mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva. But Reish Lakish does not disagree with Rabbi Yochanan, for he establishes there, in that same chapter (95a), the statement that [the mishnah] teaches, "If in a case where he had relations with a lesser prohibition, [the one who prohibits is prohibited], all the more so [if] the one who prohibits...", as referring to a yavam's waiting woman, and like Rav Hamnuna; and [see] the end of that passage. And at the end of [the chapter] ha-Choletz (Yevamot 49b), we also [see that] Abaye was uncertain whether [the halakhah is] like Rav or like Shmuel. And in [the chapter] ha-Zoreik in Gittin (80b), the versions of the Gemara disagree whether the mishnah was a refutation of Rav Hamnuna or a support for him; and there [too] he could have rejected the support as here, by establishing the mishnah as [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva, except that he rejected it from the wording of the mishnah itself. In the Yerushalmi it explains how Rabbi Yannai praised Rabbi Yochanan, as he applied to him the verses: "He who squanders gold from a purse," "My son, let them not depart from your eyes," "Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart," "Give to a wise man and he will become wiser still," "A wise man will hear and increase learning." Reish Lakish said to him: After all these verses of praise, he is able [to do so]; he could have interpreted it for him as [in accordance with] Rabbi Akiva. And furthermore, [Rabbi Yochanan] rejects him there: But let me raise an objection - what does a *mamzer* have to do with the matter of warning [the *sotah*]? The Torah said, "and he warns his wife" - even part of his wife. And according to the conclusion there, it implies that the halakhah is not like Rav Hamnuna. And so it reads there: [In the case of] a yavam's waiting woman who committed adultery, Rabbi Eliezer says: She is permitted to her household [i.e., her husband]; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: She is forbidden to her household. Rabbi Yannai said: A yavam's waiting woman who committed adultery is permitted to her household, and it was taught likewise: "And it is hidden from the eyes of her husband" - but not from the eyes of her yavam. Rabbi Yaakov ben Zavdi in the name of Rabbi Abahu: There was an incident, and she was a priest's daughter [or wife], and she was permitted to her household. Rabbi Yose bar Bun said: She does not even receive lashes. According to the Yerushalmi, it implies that Rabbi Yannai disagrees with Rabbi Yannai [as quoted] in what is said in Ha-Ishah Rabbah: Rabbi Yannai said, in a group they voted and concluded that betrothal does not take effect with a yevamah. We read it thus in the Yerushalmi: Rabbi Shmuel said: Is that not so? Rabbi Yannai said: Thirty-some elders voted - from where [is it derived] that betrothal does not take effect, etc.
